## Workflow ownership

The repository has one pull-request routing entry point and service-owned production workflows. Application owners run only when owned inputs change on main, cancel older runs for the same service, recheck main immediately before publishing `latest` (`deploy/check-latest-main.sh`), and deploy that service's `latest`. All production owners declare identical owned inputs in both `on.push.paths` and `PRODUCTION_INPUT_PATHS`. `deploy/check-production-freshness.sh` checks source ancestry and owned inputs; manual dispatch requires exact current `main`. Host mutations use the host-level `flock`; do not restore the removed Release/Build/Deploy/Tofu reusable-workflow DAG.

- `ci-gate.yml` is the only PR entry point and owns `CI / Required Gate`. It verifies PR identity, routes changed paths to reusable owner CI workflows, and aggregates affected results. Each OpenTofu root validates only when its owner is affected; validation runs `fmt`, `init -backend=false`, `validate`, and root safety fixtures only. PR CI has no production credentials, SSH, image push, production state, plan, or apply. The three data-update workflows remain separate and can dispatch CI for the exact open PR head.
- `business-api.yml`, `frontend.yml`, `keycloak.yml`, and `ai-service.yml` own their individual application image and deploy pipelines. TX images use TCR; Yecao images use GHCR. Each owner publishes `latest` only while its owned inputs are unchanged on current main (exact current main, or main advanced elsewhere) and deploys that service's `latest`; if newer main changed its owned inputs the run is superseded — it skips `latest` and deploy without failing, and the newer run publishes. Business API runs read-only consumer-side dependency probes before mutation. Keycloak retains its runtime, OpenTofu, and final verification chain. Replay parsing runs in the browser: there is no parser-worker, RabbitMQ, or MinIO owner, and none may be reintroduced (`scripts/ci/test-workflow-contract.sh` asserts their absence).
- `caddy.yml` is the independent TX gateway owner. It stages and validates Caddy configuration/assets, reconciles only the gateway, refreshes frontend trusted-peer state when needed, and verifies TLS, redirects, and required routes. It does not build an application image or depend on database/admin credentials.
- `business-postgres.yml` and `keycloak-postgres.yml` own their TX runtime and host-local OpenTofu root. `observability.yml` owns Yecao observability runtime and Grafana dashboard OpenTofu. Keep each provider, state, secrets, plan guard, and readiness check scoped to its owner.
- `komodo-controller.yml` is the bootstrap and break-glass owner for the Komodo control plane; it is the only workflow permitted to read the TencentCloud DNSPod credentials. GitHub Actions owns controller reconciliation, Docker Compose owns the Yecao Core/Mongo runtime (`deploy/komodo`), and OpenTofu owns only the controller DNS record (`infra/tofu/komodo`). Komodo must never own its own Core lifecycle. Public ingress stays with the independent `caddy.yml` owner, which publishes `komodo.wotbtools.com`, proves the WireGuard upstream first, and then requires the public answer to equal the private one — it reads no Komodo release pin, and `deploy/komodo/**` is not a Caddy-owned input. Workload adoption remains a later phase. Declarative Komodo resources live in `infra/komodo/resources/**` (K4.1), owned by no production workflow: that path routes only to the non-production `deployment` PR gate, which runs `scripts/ci/test-komodo-resources.py`, and it must never be added to the controller's `on.push.paths`/`PRODUCTION_INPUT_PATHS` (a resource TOML change may not reconcile Core/Mongo/DNS). The sync is applied by a human in the UI only: `managed = false`, `delete = false`, `webhook_enabled = false`.
- `komodo-periphery.yml` is the independent owner of every Komodo Periphery agent (`deploy/periphery`), one host per job in a strict chain: `reconcile_yecao` → `reconcile_tx1` → `reconcile_tx2`, each `needs` the previous one so an established host is always proven before a new host is mutated. GitHub Actions owns each agent's systemd lifecycle; Komodo Core owns only the Server relationship and never installs, restarts, or manages the agent that connects to it. There is exactly one lifecycle implementation (`lib.sh` / `install.sh` / `verify.sh` / `reconcile.sh` are target-agnostic) and the per-host differences live in reviewed `deploy/periphery/targets/<target>/target.env` data: `connect_as`, the host's own mutation lock (`/opt/wotb/.deploy.lock` for Yecao, `/opt/wotb-tx/.deploy.lock` for TX1, `/opt/wotb-tx2/.deploy.lock` for TX2, never a Periphery-only lock), the staging root (`/opt/periphery`, `/opt/wotb-tx/periphery`, `/opt/wotb-tx2/periphery`) and the privilege model (`root`, or `sudo` for a non-root SSH account, which re-executes through `sudo -n` and preserves only the generic credential). Each job verifies the pinned release artifact's SHA256 and stages only the verified bytes plus that host's own profile — no host downloads a binary and no host receives another host's profile. Every agent is outbound only (`core_addresses = ["http://10.20.0.2:9120"]`, `connect_as` = its target, `server_enabled = false`), so no listener exists on `:8120`, and the effective config is verified byte-for-byte against the target's reviewed config. The one generic bootstrap variable is `KOMODO_PERIPHERY_ONBOARDING_KEY` (the workflow maps each host's own secret into it; the scripts never know a host-specific secret name): it reaches Periphery only through the transient `/run/komodo/periphery-bootstrap.env`, is never persisted, and is not required once the durable `/etc/komodo/keys/onboarding-complete` marker exists — completion is never inferred from `keys/periphery.key`, which v2.3.3 generates at startup even when onboarding fails, and a failed bootstrap stops the service so no process keeps the credential. A missing marker with no credential fails closed instead of re-onboarding, and Yecao's deleted secret must never be referenced again. `deploy/periphery/**` is owned by this workflow alone and must not trigger the Komodo controller or the Caddy gateway.
- `android-release.yml`, `database-backup.yml`, `cleanup-images.yml`, `prod-diagnostics.yml`, and `tx-runtime-check.yml` keep their independent release, backup, cleanup, diagnostics, and TX read-only runtime-gate responsibilities. `tx-runtime-check.yml` is manual-only, uses the protected `tx-production` environment, serializes with `production-maintenance`, requires the exact current `main`, and copies only the four verifier/helper scripts from that checked-out SHA into an ephemeral `/tmp/wotb-tx-runtime-check-<run>-<attempt>` bundle. It derives the Frontend/Business API image refs from the running containers, executes the staged verifier against `WOTB_TX_DIR=/opt/wotb-tx` under the production host lock, and cleans the temporary bundle afterward. It must never stage production Compose/config/data, deploy, recreate, stop, apply OpenTofu, or change DNS.
- `update-tankopedia.yml`, `update-equipment.yml`, and `update-crew-skills.yml` remain independent automation entry points. Preserve their contents/PR/actions permissions and exact-head CI dispatch protocol; do not fold them into production workflows.

## Change rules

- Before changing a workflow, read its real scripts and the relevant `deploy/AGENTS.md`/OpenTofu contracts. Keep CI commands consistent with local commands and the pinned JDK/Node versions.
- Do not place credentials in workflow files. Scope `secrets.*`, `vars.*`, job permissions, and protected environments to the job that consumes them. TX production jobs use the existing `tx-production` environment; do not invent an unconfigured Yecao environment.
- Main-triggered production workflows must reject non-ancestor sources and changes to owned inputs before expensive work, then recheck immediately before staging or host mutation as applicable. Application workflows also recheck immediately before publishing `latest`: unchanged owned inputs on current main publish; changed owned inputs mark the run superseded (`check-latest-main.sh` exit 10 → `latest_published=false`, downstream smoke/deploy skipped, run stays green). Same-service runs still cancel older ones when new main arrives. Manual dispatch must remain pinned to the exact current `main` SHA. Keep TX and Yecao host locks held across runtime mutation, OpenTofu plan/apply/second-plan, and verification where the service contract requires it.
- OpenTofu ownership stays with the matching standalone root workflow. PR validation never reads production state or creates an authenticated production plan. Main workflows re-plan locally and apply the exact guarded saved plan.
- Keep the stable `CI / Required Gate` as the only required PR check. Do not add heavy, non-gating jobs to every change or duplicate PR test suites inside production deployment workflows.
- Do not restore discarded PR #380 content or architecture. It is not a source for this plan.

## Workflow inventory (35)

`ci-gate.yml`, reusable `ci-<owner>.yml` workflows, `business-api.yml`, `frontend.yml`, `caddy.yml`, `keycloak.yml`, `ai-service.yml`, `business-postgres.yml`, `keycloak-postgres.yml`, `observability.yml`, `alloy-tx.yml`, `komodo-controller.yml`, `komodo-periphery.yml`, `tx-runtime-check.yml`, `android-release.yml`, `database-backup.yml`, `cleanup-images.yml`, `prod-diagnostics.yml`, `tx-gitee-build-path-validation.yml`, `update-tankopedia.yml`, `update-equipment.yml`, and `update-crew-skills.yml`.
